mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of months when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS above 12-month moving average) signals accommodative policy coupled with robust demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong consumer demand
failure_condition: Joint signal fails: Rank IC below 0.02 over any 3-year window, or positive returns occur in less than 55% of joint signal instances.

mechanism_narrative: During high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 1.5% YoY), manufacturing output expansion supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns negative in more than 55% of INDPRO growth periods, or Rank IC below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) over the past three months indicates strong housing market activity that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns negative in more than 55% of HOUST increase periods, or Rank IC below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 2.5% for two consecutive months, it signals monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns positive in more than 45% of FEDFUNDS > 2.5% periods, or Rank IC below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS > 135,000 thousand) combined with robust consumer spending (RSAFS > 420,000 million) signals high disposable income and earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint signal fails: Rank IC below 0.02 over any 3-year window, or positive returns occur in less than 55% of joint signal instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high labor market tightness (UNRATE < 4.0%), the tight labor market supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns negative in more than 55% of UNRATE < 4.0% periods, or Rank IC below 0.02 over any 3-year window.
